issues.title: Duplicated getContrastColor helper using deprecated String.prototype.substr
issues.body:
## Problem
The same hex-luminance helper is copy-pasted in two places, and both use the deprecated `.substr`:

- `apps/client/src/components/ui/tag-badge.tsx:39-47` (three `.substr` calls at lines 44–46)
- `apps/client/src/components/Dashboards/Dashboards.utils.ts:74-80` (three at 76–78)

## Suggested fix
Keep one implementation (the `Dashboards.utils.ts` one is already in a utils module — or move it somewhere shared like `lib/`), switch `.substr(start, len)` to `.slice(start, start + len)`, and import it from both call sites. *(trivial–easy)*

issues.title: Extract the hardcoded 'jwt' localStorage key into a named constant

The auth token's localStorage key is the bare string `'jwt'` at 10 call sites across 8 files:

Renaming the key, or finding every place the token is read, means grepping for a four-letter string that also matches unrelated code.

## Suggested fix
Export `const AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY = 'jwt';` from `apps/client/src/lib/auth.ts` (it already owns token handling) and import it at every site. Behavior must not change — the value stays `'jwt'` so existing sessions keep working.

*(trivial — mechanical, but touches 8 files, so it's good practice for a careful multi-file change)*

issues.title: [RFC]: PersonaPlex multi-session serving on the unified duplex path (tick gather, batched Mimi, depformer graphs)
issues.body:
### Motivation.

PersonaPlex (`nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1`, a Moshi finetune) is an always-clocked full-duplex model: every live session must consume one 80 ms frame and emit one 80 ms frame, 12.5 times per second, for the whole call. On the unified engine path (`/v1/realtime?duplex=1`) the shipped envelope is `duplex_session.max_sessions: 2` (`vllm_omni/deploy/personaplex.yaml:18`), and the design doc explicitly does not claim more (`docs/design/fullduplex-personaplex.md:70-72`, `:79-85`). A session also cannot outlive the 3000-frame window today (section 2, item 9), so a call is capped at four minutes.

The standalone server that shipped with PR #4771 served 32 concurrent conversations on one GPU in strict lockstep (commit `2544c8f2`: B=2 28.0 ms per tick, B=8 32.6 ms, B=16 45.0 ms, B=32 70.2 ms). That engine was deleted at graduation (#6196; #6028: "PersonaPlex's demo tier is dropped rather than moved"). Nothing replaced it. The unified path is structurally unable to scale, independent of GPU capacity, because its per-frame cost is host-launch bound and most of it is paid once per session rather than once per tick.

No open issue or PR covers this. Section 9 below lists what exist

## Problem

Scopes are carried as strings (`"repository:hello-world:pull,push"`) everywhere: `ScopeRepository` builds one, `WithScopesForHost` / `AppendScopesForHost` store them, `CleanScopes` parses them apart and re-serializes them, and `Client.Do` joins them back into a cache key. Every append re-parses the whole set. Anything that needs a field out of a scope — the repository path, for #1348 — has to parse the string again.

The parsing is duplicated in three places with different rules: the `len(scopes) == 1` fast path in [`CleanScopes`](https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/blob/main/registry/remote/auth/scope.go#L197) splits on the *last* colon, the slow path splits on the first and last, and neither agrees with the other on what counts as a well-formed scope.

## Evidence: `CleanScopes` does not de-duplicate scopes it cannot parse

The doc comment promises "the scopes passed in are de-duplicated and sorted. Therefore, the output of this function is deterministic." That holds only for scopes with two colons. Anything else falls into `result = append(result, scope)` in the slow path without passing through the de-duplicating map:

```

issues.title: fetch-templates.sh fails the whole test job on one transient download
issues.body:
tools/fetch-templates.sh downloads the eight `lumenc new` templates with one plain curl each, under `set -eu`, and exits 1 as soon as one of them fails. There is no retry, so a single connection reset takes the ci.yml `test` job down with it, and the job runs the script on all three operating systems: 24 unretried downloads on every pull request that touches Rust.

Seen on the ci run for #312, where the six earlier templates fetched and the seventh did not:

```
fetching https://github.com/lumen-fx/dashboard/releases/latest/download/template.tar.gz
curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
fetch-templates.sh: cannot download https://github.com/lumen-fx/dashboard/releases/latest/download/template.tar.gz
Error: Process completed with exit code 1
```

The release for lumen-fx/dashboard carries template.tar.gz, and the same URL downloads by hand, so nothing was missing; the connection dropped. A red `test` leg here reads as a broken change, and the fix is a plain rerun, which is the shape that trains people to rerun red legs without reading them.

issues.title: getting-started.md example test cannot pass against any real target as written
issues.body:
**File:** `docs-site/docs/getting-started.md`, Step 2's `baseUrl: https://your-app.com` combined with Step 3's `Assert.assertTrue(getDriver().getTitle().contains("Dashboard"))`.

Nothing in the doc flags these values as placeholders that must be replaced before the test can run.

**Repro**

After fixing the missing `execution.mode` (separate issue), run the doc's example as-is.

**Actual output**

```
org.openqa.selenium.TimeoutException: timeout: Timed out receiving message from renderer: -0.006
```
against `Command: [..., get {url=https://your-app.com}]`. It retried 3 times total (`retry.maxAttempts: 2` working as designed) before failing the build. Nothing in that output tells a new user "the URL is a placeholder, change it."

Confirmed the test passes once `baseUrl` is swapped for a real reachable page and the assertion updated to match that page's real title — the framework mechanics are fine, this is purely a docs-example problem.

**Suggested fix**

Either use a real, stable public demo page in the example, or add an explicit callout that `baseUrl` and the title assertion are placeholders requiring substitution.

This should likely `chmod +x` the file isn't executable so that we can correctly execute the file.

issues.title: Make instrument name conflict detection case-insensitive
issues.body:
## Spec requirement
Instrument names are case-insensitive; a second registration differing only by case MUST reuse the first-seen name and log a message ([sdk.md:1017-1031](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/1377f53b2bc0683c45169b8f20fd973eb4d59419/specification/metrics/sdk.md#L1017-L1031)).

## Current behavior
`@instrument_registry` is a plain Ruby `Hash` keyed by the literal (case-sensitive) name string (`meter.rb:32,258-260` ([permalink](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ruby/blob/1fef7897fc6d38fb35fbce25fd676eae8cce29a7/metrics_api/lib/opentelemetry/metrics/meter.rb#L32))), so `create_counter("requestCount")` followed by `create_counter("RequestCount")` registers two independent instruments instead of being detected as the same name under case-insensitive comparison.

## Suggested fix
Normalize the registry key (e.g. downcase) when checking for an existing instrument, while preserving and reusing the first-seen name's original casing, and log a message on the case-differing collision.

issues.title: viewport_create_test_lab tells the caller to run execute_test_session, a legacy alias rather than the canonical tool
issues.body:
## Seen

```
tools/call viewport_create_test_lab {}
-> {"status": "created_offline",
    "scene_path": "res://addons/didi/test_lab_sandbox.tscn",
    "message": "Created sandbox scene at res://addons/didi/test_lab_sandbox.tscn.
                Open Godot Editor to view live or run `execute_test_session`."}
```

`execute_test_session` is one of the 10 legacy aliases; the canonical name is
`runtime_launch` (`src/mcp/tool_registry.cpp:601`,
`docs/CAPABILITIES.md:119`). The string is at `src/tools/visual_tools.cpp:406`.

A client that lists tools by canonical name and follows this instruction is being
steered onto the deprecated surface.

## Expected

The message names `runtime_launch`.

## Repro

`viewport_create_test_lab {}` with no editor attached.

## Environment

Didi `1.8.0+11aa42d92371.20260910T134345` (main @ 11aa42d), Windows 11,
Godot 4.5.1-stable win64 editor attached where the repro says live,
otherwise no editor (`offline_fallback`).

issues.title: project_list_export_presets errors when export_presets.cfg does not exist, instead of reporting no presets
issues.body:
## Seen

A project that has never configured an export has no `export_presets.cfg` --
Godot writes it only once a preset is added. Asking Didi what presets exist
returns a file error naming an absolute host path:

```
tools/call project_list_export_presets {}
-> isError: true
   "File is unavailable: C:/Users/.../scratchpad/proj/export_presets.cfg"
```

```cpp
// src/tools/deep_domain_tools.cpp:376-378
const auto path = root.value() / "export_presets.cfg";
auto contents = readBounded(path, kMaxPresetFile);
if (contents.isErr()) return CallToolResult::error(contents.error().message);
```

"No presets are configured" is a normal, expected state and the honest answer
is an empty list. As written, a caller cannot tell "no presets" from "the file is
unreadable", and the error text is about a file the user never created.

## Expected

A missing `export_presets.cfg` returns
`{"presets": [], "preset_count": 0, "execution_mode": "offline_fallback", ...}`.
A file that exists but cannot be read stays an error.

## Repro

Point `--project` at any Godot project with no `export_presets.cfg` and call
`project_list_export_presets`.

## Environment

Didi `1.8.0+1

issues.title: Light theme renders fully transparent with `zen.widget.linux.transparency` - dark UI text is unreadable over dark backgrounds
issues.body:
### Preliminary Checks

- [x] I have read and understood the important section above.
- [x] I have searched existing issues and avoided creating duplicates.
- [x] I am not filing an enhancement request.
- [x] I have checked that this issue cannot be reproduced on Mozilla Firefox.
- [x] I have checked that this issue can be reproduced once I removed all my Mods and Custom CSS.

### What happened?

With `zen.widget.linux.transparency` enabled on Linux, the light theme's background is rendered fully transparent. Because the light theme uses dark UI text, the interface text becomes unreadable whenever the wallpaper behind the window is dark, resulting in dark text over a dark transparent backdrop.

Setting a color for the backdrop alleviates the issue, but it cannot be set per mode. It is the same color applied to both dark and light.

Related: #6965 (transparency, fixed via #7397), #9604 (per-mode colors, closed not-planned).

### Expected behavior

With transparency enabled, the light theme should remain legible, e.g. fall back to a colored (`rgba(255,255,255,0.3)`) background so its dark text keeps sufficient contrast, the same way the dark theme already applies a darkened backdrop.

issues.title: Device artwork ignores the colour variant
issues.body:
Reported on Reddit after the v0.1.x launch thread. Reported by u/joncppl: the app shows a white WH-1000XM6 for a black pair.

## What happens

`DeviceCenterController::heroImagePath()` maps a model to exactly one image
(`apps/device-center/src/DeviceCenterController.cpp:161`), so every owner of a given
model sees the same colour regardless of theirs. The Bluetooth name does not carry
the colour, so this cannot be detected automatically.

## Suggested fix

Either ship colour variants and let the user pick one in settings, or use artwork
that does not commit to a colour. A silhouette or a neutral render would sidestep the
problem entirely and shrink the assets, which are currently the bulk of the package
size.

Separately, this mapping is an if-chain of model substrings that duplicates
`DeviceProfileRegistry::identifyModel()`. The asset name belongs on `DeviceProfile`.
